purpose: Complete the rally loop on top of the V1 scaffold. V1 built the AI worker, FSM, engines, paddle entity, and shotAdapter — but the AI currently just touches the ball without intentional placement. V2 adds the seven missing pieces required to play a full rally: (1) paddle solver, (2) interception path planner, (3) reachability gate, (4) ready position, (5) serve logic, (6) rally end detection and scoring, (7) failure mode handling.
supersedes: Nothing. Builds ON TOP OF webxr-tt-ai-integration-spec.json V1 which is already implemented.

v1_assumed_implemented.description: These exist and work. Do not rebuild or refactor.
modules: js/ai/worker.js - AI Web Worker with message router
js/ai/shotAdapter.js - main thread bridge, computes landing_x/z
v1_assumed_implemented.current_observable_behavior: AI paddle reaches ball position and makes contact, but ball goes wherever physics happens to send it. No intentional placement. No sustained rallies.

the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_1_paddle_solver: Engine outputs intent (target+speed+spin) but nothing translates intent into paddle velocity+angle that produces that shot through your existing physics. Shots have no real direction.
the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_2_interception_planning: FSM says 'move to contact point' but doesn't define HOW the paddle moves there (linear? arc? anticipatory pre-positioning?). Currently paddle teleports or jerks.
the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_3_reachability: No gate checks whether AI can physically reach the predicted contact point in time given its movement speed cap. AI attempts impossible shots, looks broken.
the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_4_ready_position: Between rallies, AI has no defined neutral pose. Currently undefined behavior.
the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_5_serves: AI cannot serve. Pro has 'disguised serve hook' specified but no serve logic exists. Rallies cannot start with AI serving.
the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_6_rally_end_and_scoring: No detection of when a rally ends (ball out, double bounce, net violation). No score tracking. No serve rotation. AI mode cannot run a match.
the_seven_gaps_v2_solves.gap_7_failure_modes: No handling for: worker timeout, solver infeasibility, unreachable ball, XR session drop, ball state corruption. Silent failures cause undefined behavior.

host_application_facts_unchanged.physics: Custom kinematics on main thread - gravity, drag, Magnus, spin, restitution. js/physics/ball.js, constants.js, collisions.js.

section_1_paddle_solver.purpose: Translate engine intent (target landing point + speed + spin) into concrete paddle parameters (velocity vector, face normal, contact point) that, when applied through your existing physics, produce a ball that lands where intended.
section_1_paddle_solver.runs_on: Main thread - it needs the live physics module to verify
section_1_paddle_solver.called_when: FSM transitions DECIDING -> MOVING. Replaces the current placeholder behavior of moving the paddle directly to the ball position.

intent_from_engine.target_x_m: Where on the player's side the ball should land
intent_from_engine.target_z_m: How deep on player's side (0 = at net, 1.37 = at back edge)
intent_from_engine.target_speed_mps: Desired ball speed at the moment AI paddle contacts it
intent_from_engine.target_spin_rps: Desired ball spin, signed (+ = topspin, - = backspin)

incoming_ball_prediction.contact_position_world: Vector3 where AI will hit the ball
incoming_ball_prediction.contact_velocity_world: Vector3 of ball velocity at that moment
incoming_ball_prediction.contact_spin_axis_world: Vector3 of ball spin axis * magnitude
incoming_ball_prediction.time_to_contact_ms: Milliseconds until AI must arrive at contact point

ai_constraints.restitution_coefficient: Read from existing js/physics/constants.js - do NOT hardcode here, import the value
ai_constraints.ball_mass_kg: Read from existing physics - do not invent

outputs.paddle_velocity_at_contact_world: Vector3 - the paddle must be moving this way at impact
outputs.paddle_face_normal_at_contact_world: Vector3 - the paddle face must point this way at impact
outputs.paddle_contact_point_world: Vector3 - where the paddle face center must be at impact (same as ball position at that moment, offset by paddle thickness/2)
outputs.windup_start_position_world: Vector3 - paddle starts windup here, computed by extrapolating backward from contact_point along -paddle_velocity for windup_duration_ms
outputs.shot_feasibility: boolean - true if shot is physically achievable within paddle_speed cap
outputs.predicted_landing_xz: Vector2 - where the ball is forecast to land. Used by reachability/verification.

pass_1_analytical_inverse_estimate.description: Closed-form computation of paddle parameters. Fast (~0.3ms). Approximation.
pass_1_analytical_inverse_estimate.step_1_required_outgoing_velocity: Given contact_position_world and (target_x, target_z) on the table surface, solve the ballistic equation for outgoing velocity vector. Include gravity and drag from existing physics constants. Iterate launch angle to hit the target with the requested target_speed at landing (NOT at launch - the engine's target_speed is interpreted as landing speed for consistency). Use simple binary search on launch angle, 6 iterations max, ~0.1ms.
pass_1_analytical_inverse_estimate.step_2_required_impulse: impulse_vector = outgoing_velocity - incoming_velocity (vector subtraction in world coords).
pass_1_analytical_inverse_estimate.step_3_paddle_face_normal: For zero spin imparted: face_normal = normalize(impulse_vector). For nonzero spin: tilt the face_normal so the paddle brushes the ball. Empirical relation: tilt_angle_radians = atan(target_spin_rps * 0.025). Tilt direction is perpendicular to impulse_vector in the vertical plane containing impulse_vector and world up. Positive target_spin = tilt face DOWN (paddle face slightly below impulse direction = topspin). Negative target_spin = tilt UP (slice/backspin).
pass_1_analytical_inverse_estimate.step_4_paddle_velocity: Decompose into normal and tangential components. paddle_velocity_normal = |impulse| / (1 + restitution_coefficient) along face_normal. paddle_velocity_tangent = target_spin_rps * face_radius_m * 2 * PI perpendicular to face_normal, in the tilt plane. Combine: paddle_velocity_world = (paddle_velocity_normal * face_normal) + (paddle_velocity_tangent * tangent_direction).
pass_1_analytical_inverse_estimate.step_5_feasibility_check: If |paddle_velocity_world| > max_paddle_speed_mps_by_difficulty, mark shot_feasibility=false and return early. Do not attempt to clip - clipping produces unpredictable shot.

pass_2_forward_verification_once.description: Apply computed paddle parameters through your existing physics and check actual landing. ~0.5ms.
pass_2_forward_verification_once.step_1_simulate_contact: Call existing collision/impulse function from js/physics/collisions.js with the computed paddle_velocity and face_normal. Get back simulated outgoing ball velocity and spin.
pass_2_forward_verification_once.step_2_simulate_flight: Roll forward through existing js/physics/ball.js until ball bounces. Record landing_xz.
pass_2_forward_verification_once.step_3_compare_to_target: error_m = distance(landing_xz, target_xz). If error <= 0.15m, accept solution. If error > 0.15m, apply ONE correction.
pass_2_forward_verification_once.step_4_correction_if_needed: Scale paddle_velocity_normal by (target_distance_along_flight / predicted_distance_along_flight). Re-verify. If still > 0.15m error, mark shot_feasibility=false. Do NOT iterate further - timing budget forbids it.

infeasibility_fallback.action: Send {type: 'request_safe_target', constraints: {max_speed: paddle_max * 0.85}} back to engine. Engine returns a center-table medium-speed neutral shot. Solver re-runs once on the safe target. If safe target also fails (rare), AI commits to honest miss (paddle goes through ball position with whatever the analytical pass produced; ball goes wherever physics sends it - typically into net or out).

telegraph_integration.rule: telegraph.js now reads paddle_face_normal_at_contact directly from solver output. The paddle visibly rotates toward this normal starting at T-150ms. Paddle angle IS the cause of the shot, not a separate indicator.
telegraph_integration.deprecation: Any shot-type-to-angle lookup table in telegraph.js V1 is now informational only. Solver output is the source of truth.

do_not: Do not hardcode physics constants - import from js/physics/constants.js
Do not iterate forward verification more than once
Do not silently clip paddle_velocity to max - return infeasibility instead
Do not call this from inside the AI worker - it runs on main thread for physics access

section_2_interception_path_planner.purpose: Plan the AI paddle's movement from its current position to the solver-computed contact_point over the available time. Replaces any current 'snap to ball position' behavior.
section_2_interception_path_planner.runs_on: Main thread, called once per rally during MOVING state

inputs.current_paddle_position_world: Where AI paddle is right now

outputs.trajectory_keyframes: Array of {time_ms, position_world, paddle_face_normal_world}. 8 keyframes total spaced across the time budget. The render loop interpolates between them.
outputs.windup_phase_keyframes: First 60% of time budget - paddle moves to windup_start_position with face oriented neutrally
outputs.swing_phase_keyframes: Last 40% of time budget - paddle accelerates from windup_start through contact_point reaching target_paddle_velocity at contact, with face rotating to telegraphed normal

algorithm.windup_phase_path: Quadratic bezier from current_position to windup_start_position. Control point is the midpoint raised 10-15cm vertically to create a natural arc (not robotic straight-line motion).
algorithm.swing_phase_path: Quintic polynomial from windup_start_position to contact_point. Quintic ensures smooth velocity at both ends - paddle arrives at contact with exactly target_paddle_velocity, no jerk.
algorithm.face_rotation: Slerp from current face orientation to neutral during windup, then slerp from neutral to telegraphed face_normal during swing. Telegraph rotation begins at the 50% mark of swing phase (≈T-150ms before contact).
algorithm.speed_validation: Compute max instantaneous speed along the planned trajectory. If exceeds max_paddle_speed_by_difficulty * 1.1, reduce trajectory curvature OR mark unreachable (see reachability gate).

section_2_interception_path_planner.render_integration: Render loop reads current time, finds bracketing keyframes, interpolates position and face_normal. Use simple Catmull-Rom or cubic interpolation between keyframes for C1 continuity (no visible jerks).
do_not: Do not move in a straight line A to B - robotic, breaks immersion
Do not teleport - paddle must visibly travel
Do not exceed max_paddle_speed cap - that's what triggers reachability failure

section_3_reachability_gate.purpose: Before committing to MOVING state, check whether the AI can physically reach the contact point in time given its movement speed cap. Prevents AI from attempting impossible shots.
section_3_reachability_gate.runs_on: Main thread, called in DECIDING state after solver but BEFORE MOVING transition

inputs.required_terminal_velocity: Solver output - paddle must arrive moving this fast

algorithm.feasibility_check: required_average_speed_mps <= (max_paddle_speed * 0.80). The 0.80 factor accounts for windup overhead (paddle must slow at windup_start before accelerating again).
algorithm.outcome_reachable: Return {reachable: true}. FSM proceeds to MOVING.
algorithm.outcome_stretch_reachable: If required_average_speed is between 0.80x and 1.00x of max_paddle_speed: AI can reach it but only with a stretch animation. Return {reachable: true, stretched: true}. Embodiment plays lunge variant.
algorithm.outcome_unreachable: If required_average_speed > max_paddle_speed: ball cannot be intercepted in time. Return {reachable: false, miss_direction: vector_from_paddle_to_ball}. AI commits to honest miss - plays a believable 'reached for it but couldn't' lunge in miss_direction. Rally ends, point awarded to player.

section_3_reachability_gate.rationale: Without this gate, AI tries impossible shots and either teleports or arrives late and miss-hits awkwardly. The gate makes misses look like real misses - AI lunges visibly toward unreachable balls.
section_3_reachability_gate.ties_into_imperfection: imperfection.js can artificially shrink max_paddle_speed by 10-20% on randomly selected rallies to manufacture 'stretched' or 'unreachable' outcomes for variety. This is how natural-looking misses happen.

section_4_ready_position.purpose: Define where the AI paddle returns to between shots (during IDLE state and end of RECOVERING). Currently undefined.

neutral_ready_position_world.description: AI's home position when waiting for opponent's shot
neutral_ready_position_world.z_m: 1.5 - assumes AI is on z>0 side of table; this is 13cm behind back edge of AI's half, neutral standoff
neutral_ready_position_world.y_m: 0.95 - paddle held at chest height, ~19cm above table surface
neutral_ready_position_world.face_normal_world: (-1, 0, 0) when AI is on right side of table - face roughly pointing toward incoming ball; flip for left-side serve handoff

anticipatory_bias.description: Pro AI shifts ready position slightly based on player tendencies. Beginner and Intermediate stay at neutral.
anticipatory_bias.pro_logic: Track player's last 10 outgoing shot landing positions. Compute centroid. Bias ready position 30% toward that centroid (capped at +/-0.20m from neutral). Updates between rallies, not during.
anticipatory_bias.rationale: Real players stand slightly toward where opponent tends to hit. This is subtle anticipation that skilled human opponents do unconsciously.

section_4_ready_position.transition_to_ready: After RECOVERING completes, paddle interpolates from end-of-recovery pose to ready position over 200ms. Smooth, no snapping.

section_5_serve_logic.purpose: AI initiates rallies by serving. Currently undefined. Serves are different from rallies because there is no incoming ball to react to.

transitions.PRE_SERVE: Trigger when AI has the serve (per scoring rules). Move paddle to serve_ready_position over 400ms.
transitions.BALL_TOSS: Spawn ball at toss origin (above AI's paddle hand). Apply upward initial velocity 2.5 m/s. Existing physics takes over.
transitions.SERVE_WINDUP: 150-300ms after toss, paddle begins moving to contact toss-ball at apex.
transitions.SERVE_CONTACT: Solver runs with synthetic 'incoming ball' = toss ball state at apex. Standard contact happens.
transitions.POST_SERVE: Recovery to ready position. FSM hands off to normal rally flow.

serve_target_selection.beginner: Center of opponent service box. No variation. Landing target = (0.0, 1.0) on opponent side. Speed 3.5 m/s. Spin 0.
serve_target_selection.intermediate: Random within opponent service box. Speed 5-6 m/s. Mild spin (-5 to +5).
serve_target_selection.pro_short_serve_mode: Probability 0.35: serve lands short (z < 0.4) - forces opponent forward
serve_target_selection.pro_long_serve_mode: Probability 0.35: serve lands deep (z > 1.0) - power serve
serve_target_selection.pro_corner_serve_mode: Probability 0.30: serve lands in side corner with disguised spin (see below)

disguised_serve_pro_only.description: Pro telegraphs paddle angle implying one spin, late wrist applies opposite
disguised_serve_pro_only.implementation: At T-150ms (normal telegraph time), paddle shows face_normal for spin A. At T-30ms, wrist rotates 25-35 degrees to apply spin B at contact. Solver runs with spin B as the actual target. Telegraph is intentionally false.
disguised_serve_pro_only.rate: 30% of Pro serves are disguised. Higher rate makes the disguise expected, killing the trick.
disguised_serve_pro_only.this_is_the_one_place_telegraph_can_lie: Anywhere else in the game, telegraph must be truthful. Serves are the exception because deception is part of real table tennis serving.

serve_legality.must_bounce_own_side_first: Outgoing ball MUST bounce on AI's side of table before crossing net. Solver target_z must be > 0 from AI side. If solver produces a direct-over-net serve, mark infeasible and retry.
serve_legality.must_clear_net: Ball must clear net height (15.25cm) - existing physics enforces this naturally.
serve_legality.must_land_in_service_box: Initial serve must land in diagonal service box (left half of opponent side if serving from right, vice versa). Solver target_x is constrained to this diagonal.

ball_spawning.do_not_invent_ball_spawn_API: Use whatever existing js/physics/ball.js exposes for spawning. If no API exists, add a single function resetBall(position, velocity) and document it - this is a host-side change requiring approval before implementing.
ball_spawning.approval_required: Confirm with host owner before adding any new physics module API

section_6_rally_end_and_scoring.purpose: Detect when a rally ends, assign the point, manage serve rotation and game scoring. Currently undefined.

rally_end_conditions.description: Subscribe to existing physics events. Use what already exists - do NOT add new physics events.
rally_end_conditions.ball_lands_on_correct_side_and_player_mi: Ball bounces on player side and either bounces twice OR goes out before player paddle contact. Point to AI.
rally_end_conditions.ball_lands_on_AI_side_and_AI_misses: Same logic, reversed. Point to player.
rally_end_conditions.ball_goes_into_net: Ball trajectory hits net plane and falls back. Point to opposing player (whoever did NOT hit the ball into the net).
rally_end_conditions.ball_goes_out_of_bounds: Ball passes x or z table edges without bouncing on opponent side. Point to opposing player.
rally_end_conditions.ball_double_bounce: Ball bounces twice on same side without paddle contact. Point to opposing player.
rally_end_conditions.implementation: Listen to existing ball state. Track 'last_hitter' (player or AI). On bounce events check side. Track bounce count per side. Use existing physics state, don't re-implement collision detection.

scoring_rules_ittf_simplified.match_format_default: Best of 5 games. First to 11 points wins a game. Win by 2.
scoring_rules_ittf_simplified.serve_rotation: Each player serves 2 consecutive points, then serve swaps. At 10-10 deuce, serve swaps every point.
scoring_rules_ittf_simplified.configurability: Expose game_length and best_of as parameters in aiMatch entry. Default to 11/best-of-5.

rally_manager_responsibilities: Track current score for both sides
Trigger serve.js when it's AI's turn to serve
Wait for player to serve when it's player's turn (player serves via existing player paddle)
Update score display via existing UI module
Detect game end and match end
section_6_rally_end_and_scoring.ui_integration: Reuse existing UI module (js/ui/) to display score. Do not create new UI primitives unless they don't exist - confirm first.

section_7_failure_mode_handling.purpose: Handle the 5 known failure modes explicitly. Without this, failures cause undefined behavior - crashes, frozen AI, broken rallies.

ai_worker_timeout.definition: Main thread requests target via postMessage, no response within 50ms
ai_worker_timeout.detection: setTimeout when sending request, clear on response
ai_worker_timeout.fallback: Use last-known-good target from previous rally. If none, use Beginner-mode safe shot (center, medium speed, low spin).
ai_worker_timeout.logging: console.warn with timing info. Do not crash.

solver_infeasibility_repeat.definition: Solver returns infeasible 3 times in a row for the same rally
solver_infeasibility_repeat.detection: Counter incremented per rally, reset on success
solver_infeasibility_repeat.fallback: AI commits to honest miss with lunge animation. Point goes to player. Rally ends gracefully.
solver_infeasibility_repeat.rationale: Better to lose a point cleanly than freeze or produce broken physics

ball_unreachable_in_time.fallback: Play lunge-and-miss animation in miss_direction. AI gets to ready position after recovery. Point to player.

xr_session_lost.definition: WebXR session ends mid-rally (user removes headset, browser crash, etc)
xr_session_lost.detection: Subscribe to xr session 'end' event - existing host code should already handle this; ensure aiMatch hooks in
xr_session_lost.fallback: Pause aiFSM, terminate AI worker cleanly, save current score to memory. Resume on session restart if user returns.
xr_session_lost.do_not: Do not leak worker on session end - terminate it

ball_state_corruption.definition: Ball physics returns NaN position or impossible velocity (e.g., > 100 m/s)
ball_state_corruption.detection: Validate ball state at start of each FSM tick. Check for NaN/Infinity in position and velocity.
ball_state_corruption.fallback: Log error. Reset ball to serve position. Restart rally. Do not crash.
ball_state_corruption.frequency_expected: Should be near-zero in healthy code. If happening frequently, it's a physics bug not an AI bug - escalate.

general_principles: Log failures with enough context to debug (rally number, AI state, ball state)
Failures must not corrupt persistent state (score, shot history)

v2_data_flow_per_rally.description: Full rally with all V2 additions integrated. Replaces V1 data_flow_per_rally.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_serve_start: Rally manager checks: is it AI's turn to serve? If yes, serve.js takes over. If player's turn, wait for player serve.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_during_serve_if_AI_serves: Serve state machine: PRE_SERVE -> BALL_TOSS -> SERVE_WINDUP -> SERVE_CONTACT -> POST_SERVE. Pro may use disguised serve.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_after_serve: Rally is now live. AI FSM in IDLE state at ready position.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_player_contact: Player paddle contacts ball. Existing listener fires. shotAdapter posts shot event to AI worker.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_AI_predicts: Main thread runs existing physics rollout to predict AI-side contact point and time. ~3ms.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_AI_requests_target: FSM enters DECIDING. postMessage to AI worker requesting target.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_AI_receives_target: AI worker returns {target_x, target_z, target_speed, target_spin}. ~1-4ms depending on engine.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_reachability_gate: reachability.js checks if AI can reach contact_point in time. ~0.1ms. If unreachable, lunge-and-miss. If reachable-with-stretch, flag for embodiment.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_interception_planned: interception.js produces 8 keyframes for paddle motion. ~1.5ms.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_minus_150ms: Telegraph: face_normal interpolates toward solver-computed normal.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_minus_30ms_pro_disguised_serve_only: Late wrist flip for disguised spin (serves only).
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_equals_0: Paddle contact. Existing physics applies impulse. Ball travels.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_post_contact: rallyManager watches for rally-end conditions: bounce on opponent side, miss, net, out.
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_recovering: Paddle plays recovery animation back to ready position over 300-400ms (per difficulty). Reduced movement speed during recovery (vulnerability window).
v2_data_flow_per_rally.T_rally_end: rallyManager determines winner of point. Updates score. Resets ball. Determines next server.

anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_duplicate_physics_constants: All physics constants (gravity, drag, Magnus coefficient, restitution, ball mass) MUST be imported from existing js/physics/constants.js. Do not redefine. If a constant is missing from constants.js, ask before adding.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_modify_existing_physics_module: All V2 modules read from existing physics. Do not modify js/physics/* files except to add resetBall() if needed for serves (and only with approval).
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_invent_new_FSM_states: FSM still has 8 states from V1. Serve adds a SUB-FSM inside the existing PRE_SERVE/serving phase, not new top-level states.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_use_libraries_not_in_v1: No new dependencies. d3-delaunay is the only library V1 added. V2 adds zero.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_skip_reachability_gate: Reachability MUST run before MOVING transition. Skipping it causes AI to attempt impossible shots and produces visual breakage.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_iterate_solver: Solver runs analytical pass + ONE verification + at most ONE correction. No further iteration.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_let_telegraph_lie_except_serves: Telegraph is truthful everywhere except disguised serves. Do not generalize the disguise mechanic to rally shots - it would break the read-and-react skill loop.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_invent_ball_spawn_API: If serve needs to spawn a ball and no existing API does it, ASK the host owner before adding one. Do not invent.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_invent_score_UI: Use existing UI module. If a score display primitive doesn't exist, ASK before creating one.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_invent_paddle_motion_paths: Use the specified quadratic-bezier-for-windup, quintic-poly-for-swing curves. Do not substitute splines, linear interpolation, or other curves. The math is specified for stable timing.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_invent_serve_legality_rules: ITTF serve rules are: own side first, clear net, diagonal service box. Do not add other constraints.
anti_hallucination_guards_v2.do_not_invent_match_format: Best of 5, first to 11, serve every 2 points, deuce at 10-10. Configurable via parameters but defaults are fixed.
